title: An old invoice reversed and invoiced again sends the new text to QuickBooks
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin (all permissions) at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919) on the What/Why QuickBooks host (for example qb1.qa.shopview.com).
  • The shop has an active QuickBooks Online connection to sandbox company {Sandbox-company-A} (for example ShopView QA Sandbox), and you can sign in to that sandbox.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} (for example S2-15102) for customer {Customer-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-WW-A12 Fleet) was invoiced before this change reached the build, as invoice {Invoice-A} (for example 10101), and {Invoice-A} is in {Sandbox-company-A}.
  • {Work-order-1} has a labor line {Line-1} with a title, a description and a tech story (for example "Replace tie rod", "excessive play", "Both outer ends worn, replaced and aligned"), and {Invoice-A}'s line Description in the sandbox was recorded as {Old-text-A} (for example "What are you doing?: Replace tie rod;Why are you doing it?: excessive play;Tech Story: Both outer ends worn, replaced and aligned").
custom_steps:
1. Open {Work-order-1} and go to its Finance tab.
  2. Open {Invoice-A}'s three-dot menu and click Reverse.
  3. Confirm Reverse.
  4. Click Create Invoice.
  5. Close the New Customer Payment window without taking a payment.
  6. Sign in to QuickBooks Online and open sandbox company {Sandbox-company-A}.
  7. Open the new invoice for {Customer-A}.
  8. Read its line Description.
  9. Open {Invoice-A}.
  10. Read its line Description.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 3: {Work-order-1} goes back to Complete and Create Invoice is offered again.
  • Step 4: a new invoice is created.
  • Step 8: the new invoice's Description reads in the new form: the title, the description and the tech story joined by " - " (with the example values "Replace tie rod - excessive play - Both outer ends worn, replaced and aligned").
  • Step 10: {Invoice-A}'s Description still reads exactly {Old-text-A}: both forms now sit in the same books for one job.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-11257; story SV-10132 (Story 3, What Reaches QuickBooks); PRD "What Are You Doing / Why Are You Doing It (What/Why)", Confluence 845348896, version of 13 Oct 2026, S3-E2, S3-N1, read 13 Oct 2026; design canvas board 1.3 (What reaches QuickBooks), 13 Oct copy; tech plan "Title and Description - Technical Implementation Plan" (dated 2026-09-23, shared by the QA lead 13 Oct 2026), FR-014; Source-verified 13 October 2026; not yet build-verified (a What/Why QA build exists; verification by the build verification session).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-E2: “An invoice that is reversed and re-invoiced after release day carries the new text on the new invoice, while the original keeps the old text. A bookkeeper can therefore see both forms in one set of books, on one job.”
  • S3-N1: “Invoices already in QuickBooks keep the text they were sent with. Nothing is re-synced, re-exported or rewritten.”
